target_customer: Consumers who want to share favorite places with friends and embed maps on their sites
problem: People could not easily share places with photos, video and descriptions, or embed such maps elsewhere.
business_model: Free consumer service; no revenue model found

founders.name: Cole Rise
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page, which lists later companies Particle, Litely and Polaroid Swing. TNW names different founders.

founders.name: Cole Poelker
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by TNW (2012-07-29); may be the same person as Cole Rise under another name, not verified

competitors.name: Platial
competitors.what: Users drop markers on Google Maps with pictures and comments; the only one with video upload in the review
competitors.traction_then: Over 5,000 maps created by Aug 2006 per its CEO; most and most detailed posts in the review

competitors.name: 43 Places
competitors.what: Descriptions and tags for locations with wanderlust ratings

competitors.name: Plazes
competitors.what: Links content to network router locations via desktop software

competitors.name: Wayfaring
competitors.what: Maps of themed routes with directions

technical_complexity.rationale: Web maps with photo and video attachments and embeddable widgets built on mapping APIs; standard engineering in 2006.

defensibility.rationale: Several similar sites existed and the August 2006 review called Flagr the least developed, with thin content; value depended on user contributions it lacked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Maps added user maps, and later check-in apps such as Foursquare delivered the social element TNW says Flagr lacked.

market_need_then: A cluster of 2006 sites (Platial, 43 Places, Plazes, Wayfaring) covered the same idea, showing interest in neogeography; the review judged Flagr had few annotated places.

branding.name_origin: TNW says users 'flagged' places, which fits the name, but no founder source states the origin.
branding.domain_note: flagr.com did not resolve from this session (DNS); no domain history found.
branding.community_and_virality: TNW remembered it in 2012 as a startup that was ahead of the curve; no community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The vowel-dropped name evokes flagging places and was remembered by TNW, but the product was the least developed in its 2006 review and no brand activity was found.

outcome_analysis: Flagr let users flag places with photos, video and descriptions and embed maps in 2006. TNW in 2012 listed it among YC startups that did not make it, saying it lacked a real social element and a way to involve venues, which Foursquare later did well. An August 2006 review found it the least developed of five rivals. No shutdown date or statement was found.
notes: Founders conflict: YC page lists Cole Rise; TNW names Matt Colyer, David Wurtz and Cole Poelker. The round rests on a single database (CB Insights: seed from YC dated 2006-01-16, no amount). Website flagr.com did not resolve. Status Inactive; no cause or date of shutdown found beyond CB Insights marking it dead at 2006-12-31 (single database). Competitor sources dated 2006-05 and 2006-08 are up to five months after the batch start; noted.
